title: Safety first
grammar: The passive: is gedaan, and er wordt
summary: Perfect passive: zijn + participle, without geworden (De dader is gearresteerd); past perfect: was / waren. For an activity without a subject: er wordt + participle (Er wordt gebeld; Er is ingebroken).
explain:
In unit B1 · 10 you met the passive with `worden`: `De dader wordt gearresteerd`, `De dader werd gearresteerd`. This unit adds the perfect and the past perfect of the passive, and the passive with `er` for an activity where nobody in particular is the subject.

### The perfect: zijn + participle

The perfect of the passive is a form of `zijn` + the participle. There is **no** `geworden`.

> De dader is gearresteerd. — The offender has been arrested.
> De ramen zijn vervangen. — The windows have been replaced.
> De brand was al geblust. — The fire had already been put out.

The auxiliary is always `zijn`, even when the active verb takes `hebben`: `De brandweer heeft de brand geblust`, but `De brand is geblust`.

All the forms together:

| passive | English |
| wordt gemaakt | is being made, gets made |
| werd gemaakt | was being made, got made |
| is gemaakt | has been made, was made |
| was gemaakt | had been made |

English "was made" can be `werd gemaakt` or `is gemaakt`. The choice is the same as between the simple past and the perfect in an active sentence: news and short reports of a single event usually take the perfect (`Gisteren is er een man gearresteerd`), a story told step by step takes `werd`.

### The same form as a state

`is` + participle can also describe how something **is now**, the result: `De winkel is gesloten` (the shop is closed). Often both readings fit, and the meaning hardly differs: `De deur is op slot gedaan` (someone did it, and now it is locked).

> Het terrein is goed beveiligd. — The site is well secured.

### Er wordt: an activity without a subject

Some sentences are only about an activity: there is no object that could become the subject. Dutch then puts `er` in the subject's place and uses `wordt` / `werd` / `is` + participle, always singular.

> Er wordt gebeld. — Someone is ringing the doorbell.
> Er wordt hier niet gerookt. — There is no smoking here.
> Er is ingebroken. — There has been a break-in.
> Er werd veel gelachen. — There was a lot of laughing.

When another element comes first, `er` may be left out, and very often it is: `Hier wordt niet gerookt`. `Hier wordt er niet gerookt` is also correct. In a sub-clause `er` stays when nothing else takes its place: `Ik hoorde dat er was ingebroken`.

### Er with an indefinite subject

When the subject is indefinite (`een`, `veel`, a number, a plural without `de`), the passive usually starts with `er`, and the verb agrees with the subject that comes later:

> Er worden hier veel fietsen gestolen. — A lot of bikes are stolen here.
> Er is een man gearresteerd. — A man has been arrested.

When something else comes first, `er` may stay or go: `In deze straat worden (er) veel fietsen gestolen`; both are correct.

### Word order

The auxiliary stands second, the participle at the end. In a sub-clause both go to the end, in either order: `dat de dader is gearresteerd` or `dat de dader gearresteerd is`.

### Watch out

- No geworden: *De dader is gearresteerd geworden → `De dader is gearresteerd`. (You may see `geworden` in old texts and in Belgium, not in standard Netherlands Dutch.)
- zijn, not hebben: *De brand heeft geblust → `De brand is geblust`.
- Agreement after er: *Er wordt veel fietsen gestolen → `Er worden veel fietsen gestolen`.
- Not het: *Het wordt hier niet gerookt → `Er wordt hier niet gerookt`.

### Compared with Ukrainian

Ukrainian has a short form for a finished action: `Злочинця затримано`, `Вікна замінено`. Dutch says it with `is` / `zijn` + participle: `De dader is gearresteerd`. And where Ukrainian says `Тут не курять` without a subject, Dutch needs `er`: `Er wordt hier niet gerookt`.

The passive with a modal verb (`moet worden gedaan`) is unit B2 · 1.

sentences.nl: De dader is inmiddels door de politie gearresteerd.
sentences.en: The offender has now been arrested by the police.
sentences.note: The perfect of the passive is zijn + participle: is gearresteerd, without geworden. Arresteren itself takes hebben, but the passive always takes zijn.
alt: De dader is inmiddels gearresteerd door de politie.
Inmiddels is de dader door de politie gearresteerd.
Inmiddels is de dader gearresteerd door de politie.

sentences.nl: De brand was al geblust toen de bewoners thuiskwamen.
sentences.en: The fire had already been put out when the residents came home.
sentences.note: Past perfect of the passive: was + participle. The fire was out before the residents came home.
alt: Toen de bewoners thuiskwamen, was de brand al geblust.

sentences.nl: Alle bewoners zijn op tijd gered.
sentences.en: All the residents have been rescued in time.
sentences.note: Alle bewoners is plural, so zijn. The participle of redden is gered: the stem red ends in d, so no extra d is added.

sentences.nl: Het terrein is sinds de inbraak beter beveiligd.
sentences.en: Since the break-in the site has been better secured.
sentences.note: Is beveiligd describes the result, how the site is now, and also that someone did it. Beveiligen has the unstressed prefix be-, so the participle has no ge.
alt: Sinds de inbraak is het terrein beter beveiligd.
Het terrein is beter beveiligd sinds de inbraak.

sentences.nl: Vannacht is er bij onze buren ingebroken.
sentences.en: There was a break-in at our neighbours' house last night.
sentences.note: Inbreken has no object that could become the subject, so the passive uses er. The perfect takes is, even though the active is heeft ingebroken.
alt: Er is vannacht bij onze buren ingebroken.
Vannacht is bij onze buren ingebroken.
Er is bij onze buren vannacht ingebroken.
Vannacht is er ingebroken bij onze buren.
Er is vannacht ingebroken bij onze buren.

sentences.nl: In dit gebouw wordt niet gerookt.
sentences.en: There is no smoking in this building.
sentences.note: An activity without a subject: wordt + participle. In dit gebouw comes first, so er may be left out; with er it is also correct.
alt: In dit gebouw wordt er niet gerookt.
Er wordt in dit gebouw niet gerookt.
Er wordt niet gerookt in dit gebouw.

sentences.nl: Er worden in deze straat veel fietsen gestolen.
sentences.en: A lot of bikes are stolen in this street.
sentences.note: Veel fietsen is an indefinite subject, so the sentence starts with er. The verb agrees with fietsen, which come later: worden, plural.
alt: In deze straat worden veel fietsen gestolen.
In deze straat worden er veel fietsen gestolen.
Er worden veel fietsen gestolen in deze straat.

sentences.nl: Het gebouw is binnen tien minuten ontruimd.
sentences.en: The building was evacuated within ten minutes.
sentences.note: A short report of one event: the perfect is ontruimd. Werd ontruimd is also correct. Ontruimen has the prefix ont-, so there is no ge.
alt: Het gebouw werd binnen tien minuten ontruimd.
Binnen tien minuten is het gebouw ontruimd.
Binnen tien minuten werd het gebouw ontruimd.

sentences.nl: Is er al aangifte gedaan van de inbraak?
sentences.en: Has the burglary been reported to the police yet?
sentences.note: Aangifte has no article, so it is an indefinite subject and the sentence needs er. In the question the auxiliary is comes first.
alt: Is er al aangifte van de inbraak gedaan?
Is er van de inbraak al aangifte gedaan?

sentences.nl: De politie zegt dat er al twee getuigen zijn ondervraagd.
sentences.en: The police say that two witnesses have already been questioned.
sentences.note: Twee getuigen is indefinite, so er comes in. In the dat-clause zijn and ondervraagd stand at the end, in either order; de politie is singular in Dutch, so zegt.
alt: De politie zegt dat er al twee getuigen ondervraagd zijn.

exercises.nl: In het hele gebouw zijn nieuwe rookmelders ___.
exercises.en: New smoke alarms have been put up in the whole building.
exercises.note: The perfect of the passive is zijn + participle, with nothing else: zijn opgehangen. Geworden is not used in standard Netherlands Dutch.

exercises.nl: De brand ___ binnen een uur geblust.
exercises.en: The fire was put out within an hour.
exercises.note: The fire did not put anything out; it was put out, so this is a passive, and the passive perfect takes zijn. De brandweer heeft de brand geblust would be active.

exercises.nl: ___ werd tijdens de brand hard geschreeuwd.
exercises.en: During the fire there was loud shouting.
exercises.note: Schreeuwen here has no object, so nothing can become the subject: er takes its place. Het and hij cannot stand there, because there is nothing that is shouted.

exercises.nl: Er ___ vorig jaar in deze stad veel boetes uitgedeeld.
exercises.en: A lot of fines were handed out in this city last year.
exercises.note: After er the verb agrees with the real subject, veel boetes, which is plural: zijn. Is and werd are singular.

exercises.nl: De nooduitgang ___ (zijn) met dozen geblokkeerd, dus niemand kon naar buiten.
exercises.en: The emergency exit had been blocked with boxes, so nobody could get out.
exercises.note: The story is in the past (kon), and the blocking had happened before: was + participle. Is would belong to a story in the present.

exercises.nl: Het verbod op vuurwerk is vorig jaar ___ (invoeren).
exercises.en: The ban on fireworks was introduced last year.
exercises.note: Invoeren is separable, so the participle is in + ge + voerd, one word. Is + participle is the perfect of the passive.

exercises.en: Have the neighbours been warned yet?
exercises.note: Zijn + participle, the perfect of the passive. Waarschuwen has no unstressed prefix, so the participle gets ge: gewaarschuwd.

answers: Vannacht is er in de school ingebroken.
Vannacht is er ingebroken in de school.
exercises.en: Last night there was a break-in at the school.
exercises.note: Vannacht is the first element, so is comes second, then er. The participle ingebroken goes to the end; the place may also follow it.

answers: Ik heb gehoord dat de dader is gearresteerd.
Ik heb gehoord dat de dader gearresteerd is.
exercises.en: I have heard that the offender has been arrested.
exercises.note: In a dat-clause both verbs go to the end, and both orders are correct: is gearresteerd or gearresteerd is.

answers: Er zijn twee gewonde fietsers naar het ziekenhuis gebracht.
exercises.en: Two injured cyclists have been taken to hospital.
exercises.note: The subject twee gewonde fietsers is indefinite, so the sentence starts with er. Zijn agrees with the plural subject, and the participle closes the sentence.

exercises.from: De dader werd door de politie gearresteerd.
answers: De dader is door de politie gearresteerd.
De dader is gearresteerd door de politie.
exercises.en: The offender has been arrested by the police.
exercises.note: Werd becomes is, and the participle stays. Not *is gearresteerd geworden: the perfect of the passive has no geworden.

exercises.task: Make it passive, starting with Er.
exercises.note: Roken here has no object, so there is nothing to become the subject: er + wordt + participle. Wordt is always singular in this kind of sentence.

exercises.from: Er worden in deze wijk veel fietsen gestolen.
answers: In deze wijk worden veel fietsen gestolen.
In deze wijk worden er veel fietsen gestolen.
exercises.en: A lot of bikes are stolen in this neighbourhood.
exercises.note: In deze wijk takes the first place, so worden comes second. Er may stay or go; both are correct.

exercises.wrong: De gewonde man is door een buurman gered geworden.
answers: De gewonde man is door een buurman gered.
De gewonde man werd door een buurman gered.
De gewonde man is gered door een buurman.
De gewonde man werd gered door een buurman.
exercises.en: The injured man was rescued by a neighbour.
exercises.note: The perfect of the passive is zijn + participle, without geworden: is gered. Werd gered is also correct.

exercises.wrong: Er wordt in de zomer veel fietsen gestolen.
answers: Er worden in de zomer veel fietsen gestolen.
exercises.en: A lot of bikes are stolen in the summer.
exercises.note: Er is not the subject. The verb agrees with veel fietsen, which is plural: worden.
